endpoints.description:
Per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) version (v) 1.1.
Progression-free survival (PFS) will be compared between treatment arms using the un-stratified log-rank test at one-sided level of 0.05 and the p-value will be used for decision making.
The hazard ratio (HR) for PFS will be estimated using a Cox proportional hazards model and the 95% confidence interval (CI) for the HR will be provided.
Kaplan-Meier methodology will be used to estimate the median PFS for each treatment arm, and Kaplan-Meier curves will be produced.
Brookmeyer-Crowley methodology will be used to construct the 95% CI for the median PFS for each treatment arm.
All randomized patients regardless of any treatment received will be included in the analysis.
Patients will be assigned to the treatment group they were randomized to regardless of actual treatment received.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT04094688 is a Phase III study of vitamin D3 supplementation added to standard chemotherapy (FOLFOX or FOLFIRI) plus bevacizumab in advanced/metastatic colorectal cancer. Primary endpoint is PFS; secondary endpoints include ORR, OS, safety, and biomarker endpoints.
Evidence search returned registry citation and general literature on bevacizumab+chemotherapy in mCRC and vitamin D mechanisms, but no results reporting actual trial outcomes as of cutoff 2026-01-31.

Bevacizumab+chemotherapy is established standard of care in mCRC with typical PFS ~8-10 months and OS ~20-24 months. Vitamin D3 supplementation has shown preclinical anti-tumor effects but prior clinical trials in CRC have not demonstrated significant PFS/OS benefit.

SUNSHINE trial (Ng et al) tested high-dose vitamin D3 in mCRC with chemotherapy; showed potential PFS improvement in subgroup but not definitive. This supports modest directional possibility of benefit but low confidence for primary endpoint success.
Safety: vitamin D3 at standard doses (4000 IU/day or less) has well-established safety profile; hypercalcemia risk is low. Expected safety signals similar to chemotherapy+bevacizumab alone.

Key risks: vitamin D3 may not add meaningful efficacy to established regimen; trial may miss primary PFS endpoint. Biomarker endpoints (25(OH)D levels, deficiency incidence) are mechanistic and likely to show expected pharmacodynamic effects.
Physical activity+PFS endpoint is exploratory with limited prior validation; prediction uncertain.
Coverage gaps: No access to actual trial results, interim analyses, or protocol-defined statistical analysis plan as of cutoff.

Trial NCT04094688 is a Phase III study of Vitamin D3 with chemotherapy and bevacizumab in advanced/metastatic colorectal cancer. The frozen endpoints secondary-6 and secondary-7 are pharmacodynamic/biomarker endpoints related to 25(OH)D levels. Secondary-6 measures baseline 25(OH)D levels (descriptive, not a time-to-event outcome despite contract label). Secondary-7 assesses prognostic effect of highest achieved 25(OH)D on clinical outcomes over 5 years.

Evidence search returned no direct results for NCT04094688 outcomes (registry 403, limited literature hits with no trial-specific results). Retrieved sources include: (1) Crossref DOI 10.31525/ct1-nct04094688 - trial registration reference, date 2019-09-19, not fetchable as living record; (2) Europe PMC 32624575 - Vitamin D supplementation in mCRC review, 2020-07-06, mechanism background only; (3) Crossref 10.2217/crc.15.12 - Vitamin D and colorectal cancer review, 2015-04-16, mechanism background.

No direct numeric evidence for this specific trial's 25(OH)D results. Evidence gaps: no published baseline 25(OH)D data, no achieved 25(OH)D levels, no prognostic analysis results. All predictions rely on indirect inference from vitamin D pharmacokinetics in cancer populations and similar Phase II/III supplementation trials.

Secondary-6: Baseline 25(OH)D in advanced CRC patients typically shows high deficiency rates (30-50% <20 ng/mL, 60-80% <30 ng/mL per observational studies). This is a descriptive baseline measure, not a comparative endpoint. Contract labels as time_to_event but measure is actually continuous/baseline descriptive.

Secondary-7: Prognostic effect of achieved 25(OH)D on PFS/OS. Prior Phase II data (Sunshine trial Ng et al.) suggested high-dose vitamin D3 improved PFS in mCRC with median 25(OH)D ~40 ng/mL vs ~20 ng/mL. Effect size HR ~0.64 for PFS. This trial uses similar high-dose supplementation (4000 IU/day per registration). Predict modest prognostic association.
Key risks: biomarker variability, compliance, concurrent medications affecting vitamin D metabolism, no established 25(OH)D threshold for CRC prognosis.

direction_consistency.reason: 证据：primary-0 模型预测高剂量/干预侧中位 PFS 9.5 months，高于对照 8.5 months；Gold primary-0 中 Arm I high-dose Vitamin D3 为 11.8 months，高于 Arm II standard-dose Vitamin D3 的 10.3 months。优点与不足：优点是两组中位 PFS 的方向一致，均显示高剂量 Vitamin D3 侧 PFS 更长；不足是模型同时给 HR 0.90 但 Gold 未提供 HR/p-value，不能核验统计显著性或 HR 方向强度。评分档位依据：方向本身匹配，基础 100；因 HR 与显著性不可核验扣 10，得到 100 - 10 = 90。
